title: Adic completeness lifts across a square-zero ideal
statement: Let $C$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $Q\subseteq C$ an ideal with $Q^2=0$, and $H\subseteq C$ any ideal. Suppose the quotient ring $C/Q$ is $(H+Q)/Q$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Then $C$ is $H$-adically complete. No section of $C\to C/Q$, coefficient-ring flatness, or locality assumption is required.

source.place: Tag 0DYC (lemma-complete-modulo-nilpotent), specialization to its I=Q with Q squared zero and its J=H. The general lemma assumes Q-adic completeness, automatic for Q squared zero.

proof.text: For every $n\geq2$, the equality $Q^n=0$ follows from $Q^2=0$. Thus the quotient system defining the $Q$-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring] has the constant tail $C/Q^n=C$ with identity transition maps. A compatible family $(x_n)$ is uniquely determined by $x_2\in C$: its terms for $n\geq2$ equal $x_2$, and its earlier terms are the images of $x_2$ under the quotient maps. Hence the canonical map $C\to\varprojlim_n C/Q^n$ is bijective, so $C$ is $Q$-adically complete.

source.place: Tag 0317 (definition-complete), applied to the eventually constant quotient system; verification of the first completeness hypothesis in Tag 0DYC (lemma-complete-modulo-nilpotent).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-two-ideal-adic-completeness] with $R=C$, $I=Q$, and $J=H$. Its Noetherian hypothesis is exactly the hypothesis on $C$. Its first completeness hypothesis is step 1, and its quotient completeness hypothesis is precisely the assumed completeness of $C/Q$ for $(Q+H)/Q=(H+Q)/Q$. The lemma therefore gives $H$-adic completeness of $C$. The cited statement imposes no section, coefficient-ring flatness, or locality hypothesis.
